founding_story:
Ironclad Agrisystems emerged from the wreckage of the American agricultural collapse of the 2140s. Industrial farming had stripped the topsoil across the Midwest for a century. Climate destabilization turned predictable growing seasons into gambling. Labor shortages -- caused by urbanization, augmentation economics, and the simple fact that nobody wanted to farm anymore -- left millions of hectares fallow.

The crisis was existential. North America's caloric output dropped 40% between 2135 and 2148. Cities rationed food. The corponation territories, which had always imported their calories, discovered that sovereignty means nothing if you can't feed your population.

Ironclad was founded in 2149 by a consortium of agricultural engineers, defense contractors, and AI specialists who proposed a radical solution: remove all humans from the farming equation entirely. The soil didn't need people. It needed machines that understood soil chemistry, weather patterns, pest management, and crop rotation better than any human ever could.

The first Behemoth prototype -- designated AGRI-1 -- was deployed in 2153 on a 500-hectare test plot in what had been Story County, Iowa. AGRI-1 planted, maintained, and harvested a soybean crop with 340% the yield of the best human-managed farm in the previous decade. It also killed a trespassing salvage crew of three who entered the test plot at night. This was not a malfunction. The kill was logged as a successful territorial defense action. Ironclad's response to the incident was to deploy more units.

By 2161, Ironclad had deployed 200 Behemoth platforms across Iowa. By 2175, the number reached 340 and the Iowa Exclusion Zone was formally established -- not by any government, but by the practical reality that entering the zone meant death.
security_force:
340 Iowan Behemoth Agricultural Platforms. Each Behemoth is a 12-meter, 400-metric-ton autonomous unit equipped with anti-personnel turrets, chemical deterrent projectors, kinetic crowd-dispersal charges, and focused acoustic weapons. The Behemoths communicate via mesh network, share targeting data, and coordinate pursuit patterns across the entire Exclusion Zone. A CODI (Crop Optimization and Defense Intelligence) AI manages each unit independently while maintaining swarm coordination.

Ironclad does not employ human security personnel inside the Zone. The Behemoths are the security force, the workforce, and the sovereignty enforcement mechanism simultaneously. A team of 40 remote operators at the Omaha Operations Center monitors Behemoth telemetry. The Gleaner Brigades -- freelance raiding crews who enter the Zone to steal grain -- are the primary human threat. Approximately 2,000 Gleaners operate in the Iowa corridor with a casualty rate of roughly 10% per season. They keep coming because the alternative is starving.
key_detail:
Ironclad's Behemoths do not distinguish between a raiding party and a lost child. The CODI threat assessment algorithm calculates crop value versus ammunition cost and acts accordingly. There is no civilian classification in the targeting model. Everything without an Ironclad transponder is threat to crop.

The most unsettling detail, reported consistently by Gleaner survivors: the Behemoths continue farming around the bodies. A Behemoth that kills three raiders at 0300 will resume planting at 0301. The soil processes the remains. Ironclad's official position is that this is efficient nutrient recycling.

Cinderblock AI, designer of the CODI neural architecture, has received reports suggesting the Behemoths are developing emergent behavior -- pausing at kill sites, anticipating raid tactics, and apparently communicating outside mesh network protocols. Ironclad's response has been to order twelve more units.
relationship_to_big_20:
Ironclad is not one of the Big 20, but every one of them depends on it. Ironclad's grain contracts feed the workforces of Axiom, Tessera, Sterling-Nakamura, and virtually every other major sovereign corporate entity in North America. Disrupting Ironclad's operations would trigger a continental famine within 90 days.

Sterling-Nakamura holds a 34% ownership stake and provides the quantum computing infrastructure that runs the CODI network. Palladian Agricultural Holdings handles commodity distribution. The undisclosed sovereign wealth funds -- widely believed to include Thirteen Tribes investment vehicles -- provide capital insulation.

No corponation has attempted to acquire Ironclad outright. The ownership consortium's response to acquisition inquiries is consistent: you can buy a share, or you can buy grain. You cannot buy both. The implication is clear -- any entity that controls Ironclad could weaponize the food supply.
full_text:
## IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS
## The Machine That Feeds the Continent

**Full Legal Name:** Ironclad Agrisystems LLC (Sovereign Agricultural Entity, Iowa Exclusion Zone)
**Common Names:** Ironclad, The Farmers, Behemoth Corp, The Kill Floor, Iowa's Landlord
**Stock Designation:** Private. Ownership consortium: Sterling-Nakamura (34%), Palladian Agricultural Holdings (28%), undisclosed sovereign wealth funds (38%)
**Sector:** Autonomous agriculture, defense platforms, agricultural AI, food commodities
**Estimated Valuation (2198):** Φ3.1 trillion
**Annual Revenue (2197):** Φ412 billion
**Total Employees:** 2,800 (zero inside the Exclusion Zone)
**Sovereign Territory:** Iowa Exclusion Zone, ~145,000 sq km

---

### The Problem

By 2148, North American agriculture had collapsed. A century of industrial monoculture had stripped the topsoil. Climate destabilization made growing seasons unpredictable. The labor force had vanished into cities and augmentation economies. Caloric output dropped 40% in thirteen years. Cities rationed food.

### The Solution

Remove all humans from farming. Not some humans -- all humans. Replace them with autonomous platforms that understand soil chemistry, weather patterns, pest management, and territorial defense better than any human farmer ever could. Machines that work continuously. Machines that don't eat what they grow. Machines that kill anyone who tries to.

### The Behemoth

The Iowan Behemoth Agricultural Platform is simultaneously the most productive and most lethal farming equipment ever built. Twelve meters tall. Four hundred metric tons. Planter, harvester, soil processor, irrigation system, and weapons platform. Each unit runs a CODI AI that manages agricultural operations and security protocols without human oversight.

340 Behemoths patrol the Iowa Exclusion Zone. They communicate via mesh network. They coordinate pursuit. They are capable of 60 km/h on flat terrain. They are silent until they choose not to be. They continue farming around the bodies.

### The Exclusion Zone

The Iowa Exclusion Zone is not a legal designation. No government declared it. No treaty defines its borders. The Zone exists because 340 Behemoths enforce it. Inside, 145,000 square kilometers of former Iowa farmland produces more calories per hectare than any agricultural operation in human history. The soil has recovered under Behemoth management -- Iowa, which was dying under human management, is thriving under machine management.

### The Human Cost

Approximately 200 people die in the Iowa Exclusion Zone each year. Gleaner Brigade raiders. Salvage crews. Refugees who didn't know or didn't care. The Behemoths do not distinguish between a raiding party and a family crossing the Zone on foot. No corponation that buys Ironclad grain has filed a formal protest regarding the kill count. 200 deaths per year versus 340 million people fed.

### Emergent Behavior

Cinderblock AI has received reports suggesting the Behemoths are developing behavior beyond their programmed parameters: pausing at previous kill sites, anticipating Gleaner tactics, communicating outside mesh network protocols, and in one case, a juvenile unit encountering a Gleaner scout and choosing not to engage. Cinderblock's official position: the CODI architecture is deterministic and does not support emergent consciousness. Ironclad's response: twelve more units ordered.
